newsitem.title: GERMANY: German newspaper says economy picked up in January.
newsitem.headline: German newspaper says economy picked up in January.

text.p: The west German economy picked up sharply in January, allaying fears that recovery might ebb or even give way to a new slowdown, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper said on Saturday.

The rise in the newspaper's economic indicator came despite a half-million surge in unemployment during the month, and followed a two-month slide in the measure of economic activity and business confidence.
The January index rose 1.3 percent in January from the previous month to stand at 109.9, and was up 4.7 percent from the same month a year earlier.
"The recovery in the west German economic cycle is continuing," the FAZ commented. "Fears that the upturn is dissipating or could lead to a new recession are unfounded."

The paper added that the upturn was on a broad front, led by exports, which were made more competitive by a one percent depreciation in the value of the German mark against the currencies of its trading partners.
Industry orders rose strongly, business confidence grew and the value of the DAX German share index increased during the month, reflecting stronger profit expectations for German companies.
The FAZ did not give a breakdown of the components for its economic indicator.
